reason: council-fact-check-remediation-2026-07-20 (Agent G ERROR G1 / Q12): marked-correct '18,800 VA' failed arithmetic and used the wrong PEC 220.42 demand-factor tiers. PEC 220.42 (mirroring NEC Table 220.42) applies to dwellings as: first 3,000 VA at 100%, next 117,000 VA at 35%, remainder at 25%. For a 22,000 VA connected load: 3,000 + (19,000 x 0.35) = 3,000 + 6,650 = 9,650 VA. Restores the original PEC Article 220 demand-load question with the corrected answer.

source_audit_support.local_source_safe_action: Corrected marked-correct option from '18,800 VA' to '9,650 VA' (council-recomputed value, matching Agent G) using the PEC 220.42 tiered demand factors (100% / 35% / 25%), not the invented 100%/40% split the original rationale used.

proposed.text: A residential dwelling in Makati has a connected load of 22,000 VA. Using the PEC Article 220.42 demand-factor table for dwelling general lighting and receptacle loads, what is the demand load?
proposed.rationale: PEC 220.42 applies the following demand factors to dwelling general lighting and receptacle loads: first 3,000 VA at 100%, the next 117,000 VA (3,001-120,000) at 35%, and the remainder above 120,000 VA at 25%. For a 22,000 VA connected load: first tier = 3,000 VA; second tier = (22,000 - 3,000) x 0.35 = 19,000 x 0.35 = 6,650 VA. Demand load = 3,000 + 6,650 = 9,650 VA. The original '18,800 VA' answer misused a 100%/40% split that PEC 220.42 does not state. Source: Philippine Electrical Code 220.42 (NEC Table 220.42 equivalent).
